label: digit 3 fed back as input during the copy phase (from the 3rd output on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the input is the token 3 (the model is re-reading its own copied 3). About 99.9% of activation mass sits on input 3. It is essentially silent for the first two copy outputs (recall_idx 0-1), and its firing rate is flat at about 2.4% for recall_idx 3 and later. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on other input tokens (a handful of tiny activations on m). Many copy-phase 3 inputs still stay inactive (precision about 0.62), and no history variable separated those cleanly: digit count, prior digits, and next output were all tried. Magnitude is largest when the next token to output is m (top examples are mostly 3 followed by m), and firing is more common in sequences with more digits.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 3, m, -, y, k, a; least: x, r, q, h) and the token being output (most: m, p, h, 1, x, 3; least: c, w, -, n); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, recall_idx=5.
